I read the whole file and checked the definitions that could compete with Mathlib. These were `IsCompat`, `heckeLin`, `heckeZ1`, `heckeH1`, `heckeZ1par`, `heckeH1par`, `qCoeffLin` and the `ρC` abbreviation. `IsCompat` and the `heckeLin`/`heckeZ1`/`heckeH1` family are specific to the project's coefficient cohomology (`coeffCocycles`, `coeffH1`, and `coeffHeckeFun`, defined in the imported Definitions files). Mathlib has no matching Hecke action on these objects. They are built with `restrict` and `mapQ`, so they reuse existing constructions rather than replacing them.

`qCoeffLin` is a ℂ-linear coefficient functional on `CuspForm (Gamma0 N) k`. Mathlib only has `ModularForm.qExpansionAddHom` and `qExpansionRingHom`. Those are additive or ring homs from `ModularForm` or the graded ring into `PowerSeries ℂ`. They are not a linear coefficient functional on cusp forms, so this is not the same concept. I found no `qCoeff_add` or `qCoeff_smul` bundle in Mathlib's ModularForms directory.

I did find a project-internal near-duplicate, `CuspForm.qCoeffLinear` in `Definitions/Def_CuspForm_QCoeffLinear.lean`. The target does not import it, and the rubric concerns Mathlib duplicates, so I did not report it.

`one_mem_strictPeriods` is a standalone theorem, which the rubric excludes. `ρC` is only a named composition. Nothing else in the file competes with a Mathlib concept. I had no way to run Lean, so I did not test any replacement.
